## What

Fixes #63310.

Multi-turn `/v1/responses` requests that replay a previous assistant turn as a
message item **without a `type` field** (with `output_text` content parts — the
shape clients such as ECA/Emacs send) were rejected with a 400 and ~239
validation errors, even though the OpenAI API accepts this exact shape.

```json
{
  "input": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "My name is Alice."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Nice to meet you, Alice."}]},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is my name?"}
  ]
}
```

Adding `"type": "message"` to the assistant item made it work, which pointed at
the pre-validation normalizer.

## Root cause

`ResponsesRequest.input` is validated against the OpenAI SDK union
`ResponseInputOutputItem`. The `input_item_parsing` `model_validator(mode="before")`
coerces an assistant message to `ResponseOutputMessage` (which *does* allow
`output_text` parts) **only when `item.get("type") == "message"`**.

A `type`-less assistant item fell into the `else` branch and was passed through
unchanged, so pydantic validated it as `EasyInputMessageParam` — whose content
parts only allow `input_text`. Every `output_text` part (and the union attempts
around it) produced a validation error → 239 errors → HTTP 400.

## Fix

In `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py`, treat an assistant message
that **omits** the `type` field the same as one with `type == "message"`:

- broaden the coercion branch to
  `(item_type == "message" or "type" not in item) and item.get("role") == "assistant"`, and
- default the missing `type` to `"message"` (alongside the existing `id` /
  `status` / `annotations` defaults) before building the `ResponseOutputMessage`.

Two scoping choices keep the change minimal (per review):
- **Omitted key only.** `item.get("type")` is `None` for both an omitted key and
  an explicit `"type": null`, so the branch uses `"type" not in item` to target
  only the reported shape. An **explicit `"type": null` keeps the base behavior
  (rejected)** — it is not treated as an omitted key.
- **String content is untouched.** A plain-string assistant item is already a
  valid `EasyInputMessageParam`, so it is not coerced.

Net: a small condition change + the `type` default + docstring; no behavior
change for any input that already validated (and none for explicit `null`).

## Non-duplication check

Searched open + merged PRs referencing #63310: the only hit is #39386
(`[WIP] Enable torch.cond ...`), an unrelated, closed-unmerged PR that merely
shares a mention. No open or merged PR fixes this. The issue's "possibly
related" links (#33089 / #35508) concern a different (message-type) code path.

## Tests (CPU, no model / server needed)

The failure happens at request **parsing**, so it reproduces with plain
`ResponsesRequest.model_validate(...)` on CPU.

New regression tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py`:
- `test_responses_input_assistant_message_without_type_field` — the reported
  case; asserts it validates and the assistant `output_text` content is preserved.
- `test_responses_input_assistant_message_with_explicit_type_still_valid` — control.
- `test_responses_input_assistant_string_content_without_type_still_valid` —
  guards the string-content path that must stay a plain `EasyInputMessageParam`.
- `test_responses_input_assistant_explicit_null_type_still_rejected` — pins that
  an explicit `"type": null` keeps the base (rejected) behavior, so the fix is
  strictly scoped to the omitted-key case.

**Before the fix** (only the source change reverted, the new tests kept):
```
FAILED ...::test_responses_input_assistant_message_without_type_field  (ValidationError)
1 failed, 10 passed
```
Standalone repro: `[no type field] FAILED with 239 validation error(s)` /
`[type=message] OK` → `RESULT: BUG PRESENT`.

**After the fix:**
```
tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py ................ 11 passed
tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py ......... 46 passed
tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_function_call_parsing.py ... 14 passed
(71 passed total)
```
Standalone repro: `omitted type → OK` / `explicit null → rejected (241 errors)` /
`type=message → OK` → `RESULT: FIXED`.

## Lint / checks
- `ruff check`: clean
- `ruff format --check`: clean
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `mypy vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py`: no **new** errors
  (the 4 `Response*Event` assignment errors at L969–982 are pre-existing on
  `main`, present with the change reverted).

## Risk
Very low. The change only alters handling of assistant input items that *lack*
a `type` field and have a list content — the exact shape that previously failed
validation with a 400. Inputs that already validated are unaffected (the
coercion target and defaults are identical to the existing `type == "message"`
path, which was already exercised for items that explicitly set the type).

## Review status
- Independently CPU-verified by @adenzhou1350 (test module 9/1-failed → 10
  passed on our head; 8 edge cases checked). Per their note, I scoped the fix to
  the omitted-key case only (explicit `null` unchanged) and rebased onto the
  latest `main` (0 commits behind); see the thread above.

## AI assistance
Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); the submitting human reviewed every
changed line and ran the reproduction and targeted tests.

         ResponsesRequest(input="hi", tools=tools)
+
+
+def test_responses_input_assistant_message_without_type_field() -> None:
+    """Regression test for issue #63310.
+
+    Multi-turn ``/v1/responses`` requests that replay a previous assistant turn
+    as a message item *without* a ``"type"`` field (with ``output_text`` content
+    parts, as clients such as ECA send) were rejected with 239 validation
+    errors even though the OpenAI API accepts this shape. The root cause was
+    that ``input_item_parsing`` only coerced assistant messages to
+    ``ResponseOutputMessage`` when ``type == "message"``; a ``type``-less item
+    fell through to ``EasyInputMessageParam``, whose content parts only allow
+    ``input_text``.
+    """
+    body = {
+        "model": "m",
+        "input": [
+            {"role": "user", "content": "My name is Alice."},
+            {
+                "role": "assistant",
+                "content": [
+                    {"type": "output_text", "text": "Nice to meet you, Alice."}
+                ],
+            },
+            {"role": "user", "content": "What is my name?"},
+        ],
+    }
+
+    # Previously raised pydantic.ValidationError (239 errors).
+    request = ResponsesRequest.model_validate(body)
+    parsed = request.input[1]
+    dumped = parsed.model_dump() if hasattr(parsed, "model_dump") else dict(parsed)
+    assert dumped["role"] == "assistant"
+    assert dumped["content"][0]["type"] == "output_text"
+    assert dumped["content"][0]["text"] == "Nice to meet you, Alice."
+
+
+def test_responses_input_assistant_message_with_explicit_type_still_valid() -> None:
+    """Control: the same assistant item WITH an explicit ``type: message``."""
+    body = {
+        "model": "m",
+        "input": [
+            {"role": "user", "content": "My name is Alice."},
+            {
+                "role": "assistant",
+                "type": "message",
+                "content": [
+                    {"type": "output_text", "text": "Nice to meet you, Alice."}
+                ],
+            },
+        ],
+    }
+    request = ResponsesRequest.model_validate(body)
+    assert len(request.input) == 2
+
+
+def test_responses_input_assistant_string_content_without_type_still_valid() -> None:
+    """String content is a valid ``EasyInputMessageParam`` and must not be
+    coerced to ``ResponseOutputMessage`` when the ``type`` field is absent."""
+    body = {"model": "m", "input": [{"role": "assistant", "content": "hi"}]}
+    request = ResponsesRequest.model_validate(body)
+    assert len(request.input) == 1
+
+
+def test_responses_input_assistant_explicit_null_type_still_rejected() -> None:
+    """The fix is scoped to items that *omit* the ``type`` key. An assistant
+    item with an explicit ``"type": null`` keeps the base behavior (rejected),
+    so we do not silently change how an explicit null is handled.
+    """
+    body = {
+        "model": "m",
+        "input": [
+            {"role": "user", "content": "hi"},
+            {
+                "role": "assistant",
+                "type": None,
+                "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "x"}],
+            },
+        ],
+    }
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        ResponsesRequest.model_validate(body)
